meta.project: Dashboard Task Manager with Google Calendar Integration

product_overview: A web-based task management application that integrates seamlessly with Google Calendar, enabling users to create, view, update, and delete tasks with real-time bi-directional synchronization. It provides intuitive calendar visualizations, multiple task views, and configurable notifications to enhance productivity for individual and small team users.
core_goals: Enable efficient creation, management, and tracking of user tasks.
Provide real-time two-way synchronization between local tasks and Google Calendar events.
Offer multiple task viewing modes including list, grid, calendar, and Kanban board for versatile task planning.
Deliver a responsive and intuitive user interface based on Material Design 3 principles.
Ensure secure authentication and permissions management using OAuth 2.0 for Google Calendar integration.
Support offline usage with queued changes and graceful sync recovery.
Allow comprehensive filtering, sorting, and searching for easy task organization.
Provide flexible user settings for notifications, display preferences, and privacy controls.
key_features: Full CRUD operations on tasks with form validation and priority, status, and categorization options.
Google Calendar OAuth 2.0 integration with secure token management and connection status indicators.
Real-time, bi-directional syncing of tasks and calendar events including conflict resolution and fallback mechanisms.
Interactive calendar views with month, week, and day modes supporting drag-and-drop rescheduling and color coding.
A comprehensive dashboard interface with user profile, notification center, quick stats, and recent activity logs.
Robust filtering, sorting, and search capabilities across task lists and calendar views.
Support for offline mode with local caching and automatic sync triggering upon reconnection.
Extensive settings panel for customization of UI preferences, notifications, and Google Calendar synchronization options.
user_flow_summary: User registers or logs into the application and can authenticate via OAuth 2.0 to connect their Google Calendar account.
Users create new tasks providing details such as title, description, due date/time, priority, categories, and status, with validation before saving.
Tasks are displayed in various views: list, grid, calendar, or Kanban, with options to filter, sort, and search tasks.
Users can update existing tasks, which triggers automatic synchronization to update the corresponding Google Calendar events in real-time.
Deleting tasks prompts confirmation and removes linked Google Calendar events accordingly, supporting both soft and hard deletes.
The application syncs changes bidirectionally with Google Calendar, utilizing webhook real-time updates with fallback polling and conflict resolution strategies.
Users can customize the application experience via the settings panel, managing preferences around notifications, calendar sync, and privacy/security features.
Offline mode supports task creation, editing, and deletion locally, queuing all changes to sync once the connection is restored.
validation_criteria: Task CRUD operations must validate required fields, enforce character limits, and show success/failure notifications.
Google Calendar OAuth authentication flow must securely obtain and store tokens, with correct handling of token expiration and user permissions.
Synchronization must be bi-directional, real-time or near real-time, with proper conflict resolution and error handling including retries on failure.
Calendar views must render correctly with smooth navigation, interactive drag-and-drop, and accurate date/time handling including time zones.
UI must remain responsive across devices and screen sizes, supporting keyboard navigation and accessibility standards.
All user actions including create, update, delete, and sync must have appropriate confirmation dialogs and error messages.
Offline mode changes must queue properly and sync accurately upon reconnection without loss of data.
Security features including HTTPS, input sanitization, XSS and CSRF protections, and encrypted token storage must be fully implemented and tested.
The application must pass compatibility tests across major browsers and mobile devices.
Performance benchmarks include page load time below 3 seconds, smooth rendering of 100+ tasks, and quick response times for search and sync operations.

features.name: Calendar Integration
features.description: A comprehensive calendar view that integrates local tasks with Google Calendar events. Features include two-way synchronization, drag-and-drop task management, and an event creation modal.

features.name: App Navigation & Layout
features.description: The main application shell implementing Google Material Design 3. Includes a fixed header with search and profile, and a collapsible sidebar with a FAB and mini-calendar.
